translations.answer: As per the IsaacLab team, falling when no motion is detected is an expected behavior, and G1_CFG is not an automatic standing controller. A locomotion policy or other closed-loop balance control must be integrated; the team recommends starting from the H1 humanoid policy deployment template. The original thread did not provide a complete strategy for G1, so adaptation and verification remain to be done by the user.
translations.applicability: Applies to scenarios where only G1 articulation/asset configurations are loaded and no balance strategy is implemented; specific versions and strategy implementations need to be verified separately.
translations.credibility.rationale: There is engineering record for the environment, processing steps, and results, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author attempted to reproduce the scenario using the tutorial and bipeds.py; the team recommends integrating the strategy into the H1 humanoid policy deployment template.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between asset/joint configuration definitions that only specify the dynamics model, and whether the scenario actually runs a locomotion or balance policy.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Integrate a locomotion policy or other closed-loop balance controller for G1, rather than just loading G1_CFG.
translations.details.environments.0: Isaac Lab's G1_CFG, create_scene.py, and bipeds.py; the original post did not provide precise version numbers for Isaac Lab/Isaac Sim.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread did not provide a strategy, training configuration, or standing verification result that can be directly used for G1; the H1 template is only a starting point.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The team confirmed this behavior is expected twice, and it is not considered a model bug to be fixed currently.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does the robot tilt forward when only G1 articulation/asset configurations are loaded? Is this a model bug?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: When testing standing strategies in real machines, use a harness, limit torque, and emergency stop; do not directly deploy the simulation asset just because it can be loaded in simulation.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The team indicated that falling without motion or balance strategy is an expected behavior.
translations.details.symptoms.0: G1 cannot maintain standing in the scenario, and all three Unitree robots in bipeds.py also fall forward.
translations.source.title: Unitree G1 only loads articulation configurations and will tilt forward without automatic standing balance.
translations.title: Unitree G1 loads only articulation configurations and tilts forward, should we modify the model or add control strategy?
